purpose: Post-Validation-16 fix (starting commit 53f72d2). Replaces the previous binary text handling (a single shared text_policy_v2 paragraph applied identically everywhere) with 3 explicit text modes, so text-risk hobbies get a mode matched to how much text their identity genuinely needs, rather than one-size-fits-all suppression language.

text_none.description: Text is unnecessary for this hobby's identity. The prompt strongly avoids readable generated text of any kind.
text_none.guidance: Avoid any readable generated text entirely - no labels, no signage, no packaging copy, no incidental text-like marks. If a natural surface could carry writing, keep it blank.

text_incidental_nonlegible.description: Text-like marks may exist naturally on objects in the scene, but must never be readable.
text_incidental_nonlegible.guidance: Text-like marks, diagrams, or notation may appear naturally on books, packaging, posters, boards, or documents, but must always be abstract, blurred, or non-legible - unlabeled diagram blocks, decorative symbols, gestural non-word marks. Never render a complete readable word, sentence, slogan, title, or brand name.

text_constrained_literal.description: A very small, explicitly whitelisted amount of short, simple readable text materially contributes to this hobby's identity. Used rarely and only where the whitelist below defines it.
text_constrained_literal.guidance: Only the specific short strings explicitly whitelisted for this hobby may appear as readable text, at small scale, never as a paragraph, a fake UI, or uncontrolled generated copy. No text beyond the whitelist may be readable.

learning.model_united_nations.decision: Chose the NON-literal route (flags/placards/semicircle desk arrangement) over text_constrained_literal, per the task's explicit 'alternative valid route' option. Rationale: asking Gemini to render specific, accurate country names or committee abbreviations as literal text is exactly the kind of uncontrolled-generated-copy risk this architecture exists to avoid (misspellings, invented/incorrect country names, inconsistent results) - the diplomatic-conference identity is fully carried by non-textual cues (a semicircular delegate-desk arrangement, generic unlabeled placards, generic multi-colored flag fabric with no readable emblem, a world-map motif with no readable place names) without requesting any literal country label at all.
learning.model_united_nations.guidance: Placards on delegate desks must be blank or carry only abstract non-legible marks - never an actual or invented country name. Flags may appear as generic colorful fabric/banner shapes with no readable text or real national emblem. A world map, if shown, must use abstract line/shape work only, no readable place names.

business.marketing.decision: Reinforces the existing campaign_planning_materials containment rule (already text_incidental_nonlegible-equivalent) with explicit anti-KPI/anti-slogan language after Validation-16 found pseudo-text/pseudo-diagrams still leaking through.
business.marketing.guidance: No fake KPI numbers, no fake slogans, no pseudo-marketing-copy of any kind, even in abstract-looking form - chart shapes and card layouts must read as clearly non-textual geometry, not text-shaped scribbles.

gaming.video.decision: Reinforces the existing generic_structural_containment default with explicit anti-pseudo-Japanese-poster language after Validation-16 found excessive pseudo-Japanese/text on posters, books, and screens.
gaming.video.guidance: Posters, book spines, and screens visible in the scene must carry no pseudo-Japanese lettering, no fake logographic decoration, and no invented readable game titles - keep all such surfaces blank or abstractly patterned only.
